data.gender_notes: Kent is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old English word 'cyne', meaning 'king' or 'ruler'. The name Kent was originally given to those who lived in the area of Kent, a region in England, as it was the name of the Saxon chief who ruled there. The name Kent carries the meaning “Strong, robust, warrior” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Kent usually hope their child will grow to embody strong, robust, warrior and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Kent has a rich history that resonates with the Anglo-Saxon and English culture. It brings to mind theImage of a strong leader, a monarch ruling over his lands, reflecting the medieval and ancient English heritage. It can also symbolize a connection to the land of Kent, with its beautiful coastline and ancient history, and the sense of pride and belonging that comes with it.
data.spiritual_significance: For Christians, the name Kent holds spiritual significance in the story of St. Kentigern or St. Mungo, the patron saint of Glasgow, Scotland. St. Kentigern was an evangelist who is said to have founded a monastery in a place called Clydebank, where the River Clyde meets the Firth of Clyde. Kentigern, whose name means 'leader of the royal retreat', is believed to have been born in the area of Kent in England. He is the embodiment of a spiritual leader and guide, inspiring positive change and growth in those around him. The name Kent is a reminder of the power of spiritual leadership and the impact it can have on individuals and communities.
